reason: The cited evidence strongly supports the mechanical and bonding superiority of Inconel 718 over other alloys under bending and hot tensile tests, but it does not provide any data or discussion on heat-transfer capability, thermal contact resistance, or thermal conductivity, which is a central premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Inconel 718 provides excellent thermal expansion matching and strong stress resistance as a transition layer between H13 steel and CoCrFeNiAl.
Inconel 718 forms a robust metallurgical bond that alleviates stress concentration and enhances interfacial stability.
Inconel 718 outperforms other nickel-based alloys (Inconel 625, Hastelloy X, etc.) in three-point bending and hot tensile tests, delaying crack initiation and plastic deformation.
Improved interfacial bonding and thermal expansion matching will improve heat-transfer capability by reducing thermal contact resistance.
The performance benefits are expected under simulated plasma-facing conditions (600–700 °C, mechanical loading).
